events.summary: Sudan's transitional government set up a body called the Empowerment Elimination, Anti-Corruption, and Funds Recovery Committee. Radio Dabanga reported on 9 February 2020 that this committee dissolved the board of directors of the Central Bank of Sudan, along with the boards of eleven other banks, over the bank's alleged links to the deposed government of Omar Al Bashir. Nine of the bank's managers were dismissed at the same time. The report names no individual board member and does not set out the evidence the committee relied on.

events.summary: The law that set up the Bank of Eritrea, Proclamation 93/1997 of 21 January 1997, puts the choice of everyone who runs the bank in the President's hands. Article 13 says the President appoints the Governor for a five-year term with the approval of the national legislature, and appoints the Deputy Governor, and that the Governor's pay is determined by the President on the Board's recommendation. Article 8 says the names of all nominated Board members are submitted to the President for appointment, that the Board seats a representative of the Ministry of Finance and the Auditor General alongside the Governor and Deputy Governor, and that a director who resigns does so by letter to the President, the resignation taking effect only once the President accepts it. The Governor may be relieved of his duties by the President for just cause after consultation with the national legislature. The proclamation sets no end date for these arrangements.
events.source_title: Bank of Eritrea Proclamation 93/1997 (Gazette of Eritrean Laws, via the Library of Congress)
